guard: a missing-export import failure names WHICH install is behind, and only prescribes `cotal ext add` when the extension is the older side
why: ONE MUTATION, AND IT REINSTATES THE DEFECT. Ranking every lockstep pair as `extension-behind`
is exactly the shipped behaviour this change removes: the message prescribes `cotal ext add` for
a skew whose behind side is the CORE, so the operator runs a command that cannot add an export to
an older core. The mutation does not merely make a cell fail; it puts the wrong remedy back.
IT MUST STILL TYPECHECK. The suite's command builds @cotal-ai/workspace with tsc before it runs,
so a mutant that fails to compile would turn the suite red at the BUILD, not at an assertion, and
red-for-the-wrong-reason proves nothing. Substituting one argument of the comparison keeps every
branch reachable and the types intact, so the red that arrives is the assertion's own.
THE DECLARED-FLOOR CELL STAYS GREEN UNDER IT, and that is the point of the anchor's narrowness.
`declaredFloor` returns before this comparison, so cell 2 still names the core as behind while
cell 1 flips. A mutation that reddened both would not have told us which input carried the
WHAT THIS DOES NOT PROVE. The lockstep ranking is only meaningful because every first-party
package moves in one `fixed` changeset group; it is gated on a `@cotal-ai/` scope for that reason
and says so in the message. It cannot rank a third-party extension against core, and the suite's
`unrankable` cells assert that it refuses to try rather than that it gets those right.
